cluster: European Union honey data: DG AGRI honey market PDFs, the EC Agri-food Data Portal API (TAXUD weekly honey imports), Eurostat Comext CN 0409 imports by origin, and RASFF/TRACES food-safety notifications. Access caveat: ec.europa.eu, agriculture.ec.europa.eu, agridata.ec.europa.eu, api.tech.ec.europa.eu and webgate.ec.europa.eu were all blocked from this research sandbox, so I fetched none of the official pages myself. The details below come from three kinds of evidence. (a) Search-engine snippets of the official pages. (b) A real Comext JSON-stat response captured from the live API on 2026-10-16 and committed to a public GitHub repo; I downloaded and inspected it myself. (c) Working, schema-checking client code in public GitHub repos dated 2024-2026, which shows the parameter and field names those clients use against the live endpoints. Each item says which kind of evidence supports it.

sources.name: Eurostat Comext dissemination API: dataset DS-045409 'EU trade since 1988 by HS2-4-6 and CN8' (EU imports of CN 0409 / 04090000 by partner, monthly, value and quantity)
sources.access_method: REST API (GET), JSON-stat 2.0 via the 'statistics/1.0' endpoint; SDMX 2.1 (SDMX-ML / SDMX-CSV) via the 'sdmx/2.1' endpoint
endpoints: https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/api/comext/dissemination/statistics/1.0/data/DS-045409?format=JSON&lang=EN&freq=M&reporter=EU27_2020&partner=CN&partner=UA&partner=AR&partner=XS&partner=BR&partner=VN&partner=IN&partner=MX&partner=TR&partner=MD&partner=EXT_EU27_2020&product=04090000&flow=1&indicators=VALUE_IN_EUROS&indicators=QUANTITY_IN_100KG&sinceTimePeriod=2020-01
Per member state: replace reporter=EU27_2020 with reporter=IT (or DE, ES, BE, FR, PL, PT, NL ...). Several reporters, partners, products or flows can go in one call by repeating the parameter.
Optional end bound: &untilTimePeriod=2026-08 (monthly periods are 'YYYY-MM'; annual uses freq=A and 'YYYY')

https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/api/comext/dissemination/sdmx/2.1/data/DS-045409/M.EU27_2020.CN.04090000.1.VALUE_IN_EUROS?format=SDMX-CSV&startPeriod=2020-01 (SDMX key order freq.reporter.partner.product.flow.indicators comes from Eurostat's own async-API example; the SDMX-CSV format value and the '+' multi-value key syntax are unverified for Comext)
https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/api/comext/dissemination/sdmx/2.1/dataflow/ESTAT/all (lists all Comext/Prodcom datasets; from the official doc snippet)

Async (only for very large extractions): https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/api/comext/dissemination/1.0/async/status/{key} and .../1.0/async/data/{key}; WADL: https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/api/comext/dissemination/1.0/async/async.wadl

Related dataset, not recommended for honey: DS-059341 'International trade of EU and non-EU countries since 2002 by HS2-4-6' (HS6 maximum; for honey HS6 040900 equals CN8 04090000 anyway). Its dimension names were not verified.
Metadata (ESMS): https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/cache/metadata/en/ext_go_detail_sims.htm
sources.cost_licensing: Free. Eurostat copyright notice: CC BY 4.0 reuse (Commission Decision 2011/833/EU), including commercial reuse, with attribution such as 'Source: Eurostat, DS-045409 (accessed YYYY-MM-DD)' and a note that Eurostat is not responsible for your modifications. Exceptions on the official page: data identified as coming from non-Eurostat sources, and co-publications. Comext-specific carve-outs reported by third parties only (unverified): CN8 data declared by Austria and trade declared by CH/LI may not be sold; data of non-EU/EFTA/candidate reporters is not for commercial reuse. For internal use in a desktop app these do not bite. Re-read https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/help/copyright-notice before redistributing.
sources.update_frequency: Monthly release around mid-month. Observed vintages: updated=2026-09-15 and 2026-10-16T11:00:00+0200. Read the vintage from the response's 'updated' field or the extension.annotation UPDATE_DATA date.
sources.data_available: Dimensions (verified in a real response): freq (A or M), reporter (EU member states plus aggregates such as EU27_2020), partner (two-letter geonomenclature codes plus aggregates EXT_EU27_2020, INT_EU27_2020 and WORLD), product (HS2 '04', HS4 '0409', HS6 '040900', CN8 '04090000'; CN has a single 8-digit honey code, so all three levels carry the same numbers), flow ('1'=IMPORT, '2'=EXPORT), indicators (VALUE_IN_EUROS, QUANTITY_IN_100KG; SUPPLEMENTARY_QUANTITY also exists but is probably empty for honey) and time. Value is in EUR; quantity is in 100 kg, so multiply by 100 for kg. Import unit value in EUR/kg = VALUE_IN_EUROS / (QUANTITY_IN_100KG*100) per reporter x partner x month. Honey varieties are not distinguished, because CN does not split honey by flower source.
sources.parsing_notes: Verified from a real response (DS-045409, captured 2026-10-16). (1) Top-level keys: version='2.0', class='dataset', label, source='ESTAT', updated, value, id, size, dimension, extension; 'status' is null or a sparse dict of flags. (2) 'value' is a SPARSE dict keyed by the flat cell index as a string, e.g. {'23': 38312341.0, '11': 1482393696}. Missing cells mean no data, not zero. (3) Flat index is row-major over id order ['freq','reporter','partner','product','flow','indicators','time'], last dimension fastest: idx = sum(pos_k * prod(size[k+1:])). Positions come from dimension[d].category.index, a dict {code: position}. Some clients also accept a list form; handle both. (4) Categories come back SORTED, not in request order, so always map through category.index. (5) The time dimension can include future or empty months, listed under extension['positions-with-no-data']['time']. Drop them and do not zero-fill; prefer sinceTimePeriod/untilTimePeriod over lastTimePeriod. (6) Comext geonomenclature, not pure ISO: Serbia is 'XS' (not RS), Kosovo 'XK', UK 'GB'. Greece as reporter is probably 'GR', not 'EL' (unverified; check the codelist). (7) Extra-EU imports are attributed by country of ORIGIN; intra-EU imports by country of CONSIGNMENT, so Chinese honey re-dispatched from BE/DE appears as intra-EU in IT's data. For origin analysis use partner codes of non-EU countries or EXT_EU27_2020. (8) The response contains aggregates, so never sum across all reporters; use reporter=EU27_2020 for the EU total. (9) Recent months are preliminary and are revised until about October of the following year, so re-fetch the last 24 months on every release. (10) Requests above 5,000,000 cells error out; between 500k and 5M cells the API returns an async warning {'warning':{'status':413,'label':'ASYNCHRONOUS_RESPONSE...'}}. A honey query is tiny (about 1 x 10 x 1 x 1 x 2 x 80 cells), so you will not hit this. Keep the URL under about 4 KB. (11) Send header Accept: application/json and use a timeout of at least 60 s.
sources.honey_specific_codes: CN8 04090000 (natural honey; the only CN8 under HS 0409); HS4 0409; HS6 040900. Partner codes for the key origins: CN, UA, AR, XS (Serbia), BR, VN, IN, MX, TR, MD, UY, CL, TH. Aggregates: EXT_EU27_2020, INT_EU27_2020, WORLD. Reporter: EU27_2020 or single member states (IT, DE, ES, BE, FR, PL, PT, NL ...).
sources.publication_lag: About 6-7 weeks: the mid-month release carries data up to about month M-2, and the latest month can be incomplete for some reporters (e.g. 2026-05 was still partial in mid-July 2026). Figures are preliminary until about October of year+1.
sources.rate_limits: No published per-IP quota found. Be polite: 1 request every 1-2 s, a few dozen calls per refresh. Extraction cap is 5M cells; 500k-5M cells goes async.

sources.name: EC Agri-food Data Portal (agridata) REST API: weekly TAXUD customs-surveillance imports/exports, sector 'Honey'. This is the only honey data in the API: there is NO honey price endpoint.
endpoints: https://api.tech.ec.europa.eu/agrifood/api/taxud/weeklyData/sectors (returns a JSON list of sector names; the official doc example includes "Honey")
https://api.tech.ec.europa.eu/agrifood/api/taxud/weeklyData/import?sectors=Honey&marketingYears=2025,2026
https://api.tech.ec.europa.eu/agrifood/api/taxud/weeklyData/import?sectors=Honey&marketingYears=2026&memberStateCodes=IT,DE,ES&partnerCodes=CN,UA,AR
https://api.tech.ec.europa.eu/agrifood/api/taxud/weeklyData/import?sectors=Honey&marketingYears=2026&importCategories=Import%20-%20preferential&importCategories=Import%20-%20most%20favoured%20nation
https://api.tech.ec.europa.eu/agrifood/api/taxud/weeklyData/export?sectors=Honey&marketingYears=2026
https://api.tech.ec.europa.eu/agrifood/api/taxud/weeklyData/export/products (lists valid 'products' filter values; an import/products twin is assumed by symmetry and unverified)
OpenAPI spec (machine-readable list of all ~116 paths and params; fetch it at app start to self-verify): https://api.tech.ec.europa.eu/agrifood/v3/api-docs
Docs: https://agridata.ec.europa.eu/extensions/API_Documentation/taxud.html and https://agridata.ec.europa.eu/extensions/API_Documentation/API-Guide.html
Legacy host https://www.ec.europa.eu/agrifood/api/... now 302-redirects to api.tech.ec.europa.eu
sources.cost_licensing: Free. Covered by the Commission reuse policy (Decision 2011/833/EU; CC BY 4.0 by default under C(2019) 1655), with attribution 'Source: European Commission, DG AGRI Agri-food Data Portal (TAXUD surveillance data)'. I did not read the agridata legal notice itself, so treat the licence detail as remembered. The portal warns that values come from customs declarations and are subject to change without notice. Automated access is not explicitly restricted in anything I found.
sources.update_frequency: Weekly reference periods (Monday-Sunday weeks). The portal refresh cadence was not verified; it is probably weekly.
sources.data_available: Extra-EU trade only (surveillance data has no intra-EU flows), by member state x partner country x CN8 / TARIC10 x week x marketing year. Measures: kg, euroValue, plus a coefficient and kgEquivalent (= kg x coefficient; for honey probably 1). You can compute a weekly import unit value in EUR/kg by origin, which runs well ahead of Comext. Can also be split by import category (preferential vs MFN), useful for Ukraine DCFTA quota flows. Coverage includes all of CN chapters 1-24 and runs from marketing year 2017/2018 (per the portal's 'what's new' note, unverified). Price endpoints exist for cereals, oilseeds, rice, sugar, olive oil, wine, fruit and vegetables, beef, pigmeat, sheep and goat, poultry/eggs, dairy, raw milk, fertiliser and organic, but NOT honey. Parameters such as memberStateCodes, categories 'Acacia' or 'Multiflower' do not exist for honey.
sources.parsing_notes: Response is a JSON array of flat objects. Field names that third-party code checks against the live API before parsing: sector, marketingYear (string, e.g. '2025' for calendar-year sectors or '2024/2025' for split marketing years), week (int), memberStateCode, partnerCode, product, cn8ProductCode, taric10ProductCode, kg (number), euroValue (number); optional procedure and preference. Also seen in other clients: memberStateName, kgEquivalent; the docs mention coefficient. UNVERIFIED field names: partnerName, importCategory. Gotchas: (1) Use httpx with follow_redirects=True if you ever hit the legacy www.ec.europa.eu host; httpx does not follow redirects by default. Better to call api.tech.ec.europa.eu directly. (2) Filters that match nothing return HTTP 404 'No results found' rather than []; treat 404 as empty. (3) Multi-value filters are comma-separated (memberStateCodes=IT,DE); importCategories is repeated in the one notebook example. (4) Spaces in values must be URL-encoded (Import%20-%20preferential). (5) Default sort is marketingYear desc, week desc, memberStateName asc, TARIC10 asc. (6) Week-to-date: for calendar marketing years, week N maps to the ISO week (one client maps ('2025', week 9) to Sunday 2025-03-02). Weeks 1 and 53 straddle years, so be careful. (7) Possible duplicate rows with conflicting kg; deduplicate on all dimension columns and flag conflicts. (8) Member state 'EL' = Greece and 'UK' may appear in older years; map them to ISO. Partner codes may include non-ISO customs pseudo-codes (QP, QW ...). (9) Data are provisional customs-surveillance figures and will not exactly match Comext. (10) For price endpoints (not honey), prices are strings like '€265,23' or '€53.49' with mixed decimal separators, and dates are dd/mm/yyyy (beginDate, endDate) — irrelevant for honey but useful if you reuse the client. (11) Unfiltered responses can be several MB, so always filter by sector and year.
sources.honey_specific_codes: sectors=Honey (exact string, capital H; confirm via /taxud/weeklyData/sectors). cn8ProductCode 04090000; taric10ProductCode probably 0409000000 (unverified). The 'products' filter takes product NAMES, not codes; get them from the products endpoint. The honey product name was not verified.
sources.publication_lag: Weekly data; exact lag not verified (likely 1-3 weeks). This is far fresher than Comext (about 6-7 weeks).
sources.rate_limits: None documented in what I found. Clients use 1 s sleeps and 4-6 minute timeouts for large pulls. Keep it to a few calls per run.

sources.name: DG AGRI 'Honey Market Presentation' / 'Honey market overview' PDFs (EC honey page) plus Civil Dialogue Group (CDG) minutes
endpoints: https://agriculture.ec.europa.eu/farming/animal-products/honey_en (current honey page; lists 'Honey market overview (January 2026)', dated 29 Jan 2026, PDF of about 1.67 MB; filename not captured)
Older path, probably redirecting: https://agriculture.ec.europa.eu/food-farming-fisheries/animals-and-animal-products/animal-products/honey_en
https://agriculture.ec.europa.eu/document/download/c04a9774-5ba3-41f5-b256-08396b2888ec_en?filename=market-presentation-honey_spring2024_en.pdf

https://agriculture.ec.europa.eu/document/download/c04a9774-5ba3-41f5-b256-08396b2888ec_en?filename=market-presentation-honey_autumn2024_en.pdf (same document UUID as spring 2024, so the Commission replaces the file in place: track by filename + sha256)
CDG Animal Production (beekeeping) minutes example: https://agriculture.ec.europa.eu/document/download/495116d9-0fee-4fad-b74c-643ee454b69b_en?filename=cdg-animal-production-2024-10-08-minutes_en.pdf
URL template: https://agriculture.ec.europa.eu/document/download/{uuid}_en?filename={slug}_en.pdf. Discover new ones by scraping the honey page for hrefs containing '/document/download/' and 'honey'.
sources.cost_licensing: Free. Commission website content is reusable with attribution under Decision 2011/833/EU (CC BY 4.0 by default), unless a document says otherwise. Charts may embed third-party data (FAO, Eurostat), so attribute those too. Remembered, not re-read.
sources.update_frequency: Irregular, roughly twice a year (spring/autumn editions tied to CDG Beekeeping / Expert Group meetings). Editions seen: 2019, spring 2021, spring and autumn 2023, spring and autumn 2024, January 2026. I found no interactive DG AGRI honey dashboard and no honey market observatory; the observatories cover milk, meat, sugar, crops, fruit and vegetables, and wine.
sources.data_available: Slide decks covering EU production (t) by member state, hive and beekeeper numbers, and member-state-reported honey prices (EU average multifloral price at production site and in bulk to wholesalers, EUR/kg). Examples: 6.46 and 3.79 EUR/kg for 2018 data; a spring 2024 deck gives about 6.51 and 5.98 EUR/kg production-site and about 2.92 and 3.69 EUR/kg bulk for 2022/2024. These are reported annually by member states under Implementing Reg. (EU) 2022/1475 (previously 2015/1368). The decks also cover production costs, world production (FAO), EU imports by origin (volume and import unit value in EUR/kg, from Comext), exports, self-sufficiency (about 60-63%), and Ukraine ATM/DCFTA notes. CDG minutes add narrative figures, e.g. 'import unit values 1.89 EUR/kg (-13.7% y/y) H1 2024; export unit value 5.74 EUR/kg'. Variety-level prices (acacia etc.) were not confirmed in any snippet.
sources.parsing_notes: Search snippets indicate the PDF text layer is mostly slide headings, with numbers sitting in charts. Expect pdfplumber to extract titles, footnotes and some tables, but not reliable time series. Treat the PDFs as documents to archive, version (sha256) and summarise, not as a structured feed. Import price-per-kg series in the decks are Comext-derived, so compute them yourself from DS-045409. Detect new editions by fetching the honey page, regex-matching '/document/download/[0-9a-f-]{36}_en\?filename=[^"']*honey[^"']*\.pdf', and comparing filename and sha256 against stored copies. Filenames are not predictable (spring2024, autumn2024, an unknown name for the January 2026 overview). Some links carry &prefLang=xx; strip it.
sources.honey_specific_codes: Filename slugs: market-presentation-honey_{season}{year}_en.pdf; document UUID c04a9774-5ba3-41f5-b256-08396b2888ec reused across 2024 editions. Legal basis of the price reporting: Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2022/1475.
sources.publication_lag: Member-state price and production data lag 1-2 years (annual reporting). Trade slides lag the Comext data by a few months.
sources.rate_limits: Static pages and files; check monthly at most.
sources.sample_response: PDF slide layout (RECONSTRUCTED from snippets): title slide 'Honey Market Presentation - <meeting/date>'; sections 'EU production', 'Beehives by Member State', 'Honey prices (production site / bulk wholesale, EUR/kg) - Source: Member States notifications under Reg. 2022/1475', 'EU imports by origin (t) - Source: Eurostat COMEXT', 'Import unit value by origin (EUR/kg)', 'EU exports', 'Self-sufficiency ~63%'. Chart-heavy, with little tabular text.

sources.name: RASFF Window public backend (undocumented JSON API behind https://webgate.ec.europa.eu/rasff-window/) for honey food-safety notifications
sources.access_method: REST API (undocumented; POST JSON for search, GET for detail and lookups). No RSS found; the old RASFF portal RSS was not found in any current source.
endpoints: POST https://webgate.ec.europa.eu/rasff-window/backend/public/notification/search/consolidated/en/  body: {"parameters":{"pageNumber":1,"itemsPerPage":50},"productCategory":[18451],"ecValidDateFrom":"01-01-2025 00:00:00"}

Origin filter variant: {"parameters":{"pageNumber":1,"itemsPerPage":50},"productCategory":[18451],"originCountry":[5075]} (5075 = China; country ids are RASFF-internal, not ISO; the API rejects ISO codes with ERR-1003)
GET https://webgate.ec.europa.eu/rasff-window/backend/public/notification/view/id/{notifId}/en/  (detail: product, hazards, analytical results, measures; some return 401/404 = no public detail)

Lookups (GET): .../backend/public/productCategory/list/en/ (key 'productCategories'), .../hazardCategory/list/en/ ('hazardCategories'), .../country/list/ ('countries': id, englishShortName, alpha2Code), .../notificationClassification/list/en/, .../riskDecision/list/en/, .../productType/list/en/ (answers under 'notificationTypes'), .../notificationBasis/list/en/, .../actionTaken/list/en/
POST .../backend/public/notification/search/export/en/ (bulk export; about 21 MB unfiltered; same body shape)
Human link per notification: https://webgate.ec.europa.eu/rasff-window/screen/notification/{notifId}
Pre-2021 history: https://data.europa.eu/data/datasets/restored_rasff (XLSX 'RASFF notifications pre-2021 public information')
TRACES NT: there is no public API or open dataset of consignments or certificates; it is login-only for competent authorities and operators (from memory).
sources.auth: none. Clients send headers Content-Type: application/json, Accept: application/json, text/plain, */*, Origin: https://webgate.ec.europa.eu, Referer: https://webgate.ec.europa.eu/rasff-window/screen/list (or /screen/search), X-Requested-With: XMLHttpRequest. Without Origin/Referer/X-Requested-With some clients reported 403.
sources.cost_licensing: Free public information. The RASFF annual report states reuse under Commission Decision 2011/833/EU and CC BY 4.0 unless otherwise noted; attribute 'Source: European Commission, RASFF Window'. The endpoint is NOT an officially documented API: it can change without notice and its terms on automated access are not stated. Keep request rates low and do not republish notifications in bulk. Public notifications omit brands and operators by design, and only notifications from 2020 onward are searchable.
sources.update_frequency: Continuous; notifications are validated daily (Brussels time). Poll once a day.
sources.data_available: List level: notifId (int), reference ('2026.3863'), ecValidationDate ('dd-mm-yyyy HH:MM:SS', Brussels local time, no time zone), subject (e.g. '<hazard> in honey from <country>'), notifyingCountry {organizationName, isoCode}, originCountries [{organizationName, isoCode}], productCategory {description}, productType {description}, notificationClassification {description}, riskDecision {description}; plus totalPages and totalElements. Detail level: id, notificationBasis, product {description, productCategory, distributionStatus, hazards[{name, hazardCategory{description}, analyticalResult, unit, maxPermittedLvl (one client reads maxPermittedLvlQuantities / maxPermittedLvlUnit instead), samplingDate}], measures[{takenBy{isoCode}, actionTaken{description}}], relatedProducts[]}, risk {riskDecision}, lastUpdate. Typical honey hazards: chloramphenicol and other veterinary residues, adulteration with sugar syrups, pesticide residues.
sources.parsing_notes: (1) itemsPerPage: one careful client reports the backend REJECTS values of 100 and above, while two others use 100. Use 50. (2) Paging lives under 'parameters'; filters sit at the top level of the body. Unused filters can be null or omitted. Known filter keys: productCategory [ids], originCountry [ids], notifyingCountry, distributionCountry, hazardCategory, notificationClassification, riskDecision, notificationType, notificationStatus, notificationBasis, actionTaken, notificationReference, subjectSearch (FoodSafe) or subject (another client) for free text (unverified which works), and ecValidDateFrom 'dd-mm-yyyy 00:00:00'. Combining productCategory with ecValidDateFrom is unverified. (3) Category 18451 = 'honey and royal jelly', which also covers royal jelly, pollen and propolis. Also keyword-filter subject for 'honey'. Re-check the id at startup via productCategory/list/en/. (4) Dates use the dd-mm-yyyy format, NOT ISO. (5) Detail URLs accept only the integer notifId; the reference form returns ERR-1004. (6) Rate limiting observed: an X-Rate-Limit-Remaining response header, and HTTP 429. One client keeps 3 s between requests, pauses 60 s when remaining < 10, and pauses 15 min on 429. A 200 response with an empty or non-JSON body happens occasionally, so retry. (7) Results are sorted newest first; stop paging once you hit already-stored notifIds. (8) Wrap the parser in a schema contract test and fail loudly on missing keys, since this API is undocumented. (9) Monthly JRC/EU Agri-Food Fraud Network 'food fraud suspicion' summaries (republished by AGRINFO) list honey adulteration suspicions not always in RASFF; this is a separate, PDF/HTML source.
sources.honey_specific_codes: productCategory id 18451 = 'honey and royal jelly' (from the live dictionary as of 2026-10-25). Origin country ids: China 5075, Ukraine 5228, Argentina 5044, Serbia 5200, Brazil 5062, Vietnam 5237, India 5118, Mexico 5151, Moldova 5153, Türkiye 5223, US 5230, Italy 5020. Hazard category ids: 21796 residues of veterinary medicinal products, 21797 adulteration / fraud, 21795 pesticide residues, 21793 composition. Classification ids: 305 border rejection, 306 alert, 303/304 information, 301 non-compliance, 302 news.
sources.publication_lag: Same day to a few days after EC validation.
sources.rate_limits: Undocumented, but enforced (X-Rate-Limit-Remaining header, HTTP 429). Use 3 s or more between requests and a daily incremental run.

sources.name: Eurostat Comext bulk monthly files (fallback / backfill for full CN8 detail)
endpoints: https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/api/dissemination/files?file=comext%2FCOMEXT_DATA%2FPRODUCTS%2Ffull_v2_<YYYYMM>.7z
sources.cost_licensing: Same as the Comext API: Eurostat CC BY 4.0 with the Comext exceptions noted above.
sources.data_available: Every reporter x partner x CN8 x flow for one month: 18 columns including REPORTER, PARTNER, TRADE_TYPE, PRODUCT_NC, FLOW, PERIOD, VALUE_EUR, plus quantity columns (exact quantity column names unverified). Each file is about 2.1 M import rows per month.
sources.parsing_notes: Needs py7zr. Filter PRODUCT_NC == '04090000'. PRODUCT_NC also contains 'XX'-suffixed hierarchical subtotals (e.g. '01XXXXXX'); keep only 8-digit leaves to avoid double counting. Partner codes include non-country specials (stores/provisions, secret, not specified) and territories (XS Serbia, XK Kosovo, XC Ceuta, XL Melilla). Heavy (hundreds of MB per year), so use it only if the API is unavailable; for honey the API is sufficient.
sources.rate_limits: Large files; download each once per release.

recommendation:
Integrate these in the following order.

1) FIRST: Eurostat Comext DS-045409 through the statistics/1.0 JSON-stat endpoint. It is the backbone 'EU import price per kg by origin' series, it is the most stable and best-licensed source (CC BY 4.0, no key), and its structure is confirmed by a real 2026-10-16 response.
- Implementation: one httpx GET per reporter set, e.g. reporter=EU27_2020 plus IT, DE, ES, BE, FR, PL, PT and NL.
  - Parameters: product=04090000, flow=1, indicators=VALUE_IN_EUROS and QUANTITY_IN_100KG, freq=M, sinceTimePeriod = 36 months back.
  - Partners: CN, UA, AR, XS, BR, VN, IN, MX, TR, MD, UY, CL, TH and EXT_EU27_2020.
- Parse the sparse 'value' dict with stride arithmetic over 'id' and 'size', always mapping codes through category.index.
- Store tidy rows: reporter, partner, period, eur, kg = q100kg*100, unit_value = eur/kg, plus source_updated = the response's 'updated' value.
- Schedule: a daily cheap check (or just around the 15th-18th of each month) that compares 'updated' with the stored value. On a change, re-pull the last 24 months, because preliminary figures get revised.
- Gotchas to unit-test against the saved real sample: Serbia is XS; partner categories come back sorted; empty future months must be dropped, never zero-filled.

2) SECOND: Agri-food Data Portal TAXUD weekly surveillance, sector 'Honey'. GET https://api.tech.ec.europa.eu/agrifood/api/taxud/weeklyData/import?sectors=Honey&marketingYears=<this and previous year>.
- Value: weekly extra-EU honey imports by member state x origin x TARIC with kg and euroValue. That gives a weekly EUR/kg unit value per origin about 5+ weeks ahead of Comext, the best near-real-time EU honey import price signal. The API has no honey price endpoint at all; this is the only honey data it holds.
- Mark these figures 'provisional' and reconcile them against Comext monthly.
- Because the field names come from third-party code rather than official docs, add a startup probe. On first run, GET /taxud/weeklyData/sectors and assert 'Honey' is present. Fetch /agrifood/v3/api-docs and log the parameter list. Validate the required keys (marketingYear, week, memberStateCode, partnerCode, cn8ProductCode, kg, euroValue) and fail loudly if any are missing.
- Treat HTTP 404 as 'no data' and call the api.tech host directly, since httpx does not follow redirects by default.
- Useful split: importCategories 'Import - preferential' vs 'Import - most favoured nation' isolates Ukrainian DCFTA-quota honey. The honey TRQ was raised to 35,000 t from 29 Oct 2025 per Ukrainian sources; the earlier order number was 09.6730. TARIC quota utilisation is a separate source worth adding later.

3) THIRD: RASFF Window honey notifications as an alert feed (adulteration and residue risk by origin, e.g. chloramphenicol in Chinese or Ukrainian honey).
- Daily POST to .../notification/search/consolidated/en/ with productCategory [18451], ecValidDateFrom = 14 days back, itemsPerPage 50, and the browser-like headers (Origin, Referer, X-Requested-With).
- Keep at least 3 s between calls. Upsert by notifId; fetch detail only for new IDs.
- Link users to https://webgate.ec.europa.eu/rasff-window/screen/notification/{notifId}.
- It is undocumented, so isolate it behind a contract test and degrade gracefully.
- TRACES has no public data. RASFF (2020 onward) plus the data.europa.eu pre-2021 XLSX is the full public picture.

4) FOURTH: DG AGRI honey market PDFs. A monthly scrape of https://agriculture.ec.europa.eu/farming/animal-products/honey_en for '/document/download/...honey...pdf' links; download, sha256 and archive anything new, then run pdfplumber to extract headline text.
- Use them for member-state-reported production-site and bulk-wholesale prices (annual, multifloral EU average), production and self-sufficiency context, and analyst narrative. Do not treat them as a machine series: the numbers are mostly inside charts.
- There is no DG AGRI honey dashboard or market observatory to integrate.

Cross-cutting:
- Attribution strings: 'Source: Eurostat (DS-045409)'; 'Source: European Commission, Agri-food Data Portal / RASFF Window'.
- Set a descriptive User-Agent and per-source politeness delays.
- Keep a raw-response cache with sha256 so revisions are auditable.
- Since the developer cannot hit these hosts from the sandbox, ship the reconstructed samples above as test fixtures. Mark the reconstructed fields, so the first live run on the desktop PC can confirm or adjust them through the startup probes.
